note: Review of three desk updates: Rennes duplicate rewritten around its new details, Le Monde blockade-count item corrected (dated Nov 3, Monday and Tuesday figures separated, outlet name fixed), Drôme/Ardèche item rewritten with accurate attribution.

ops.find: French unions said they will keep the planned

event.label: reported
event.text: France: unions say a nationwide strike on November 5 is shaping up to be large, with the CGT counting 1,140 strike notices across its organisations, Ouest-France reports. In Rennes, local unions have counted 45 specific strike calls across sectors, from rail to health and education, and want to keep their march route despite the prefecture's ban.

ops.find: The education ministry said 40 high schools were blocked on Monday and 48 on Tuesday

event.label: disputed
event.text: France: the education ministry counted 40 of 3,700 high schools blocked on Monday, while the USL student union claimed 196, Le Monde reports. Minister Édouard Geffray called the blockades "clearly residual"; the heads' union SNPDEN-UNSA counted 35 schools in Paris alone blocked in whole or part on Tuesday. The ministry has not said what its figure covers.

event.label: reported
event.text: France: ahead of the November 5 strike, the towns of Romans-sur-Isère and Valence say they will keep schools open for pupils where at least 25% of teachers strike, with canteens closed and children bringing their own meals, ici (Radio France) reports. Unions plan marches in Valence and Montélimar, and rallies across Ardèche; pupils plan early blockades outside several high schools in the area.
